nodes.title: Kubernetes Deployment strategies: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A Kubernetes Deployment manages rolling updates and rollbacks for stateless Pods. CKAD exams test strategy types, rollout commands, and how resource limits interact with scheduling.

flashcards.back: RollingUpdate: gradually replaces old Pods with new ones (zero downtime). Recreate: terminates all old Pods before starting new ones (brief downtime).

flashcards.front: maxSurge and maxUnavailable — what do they control?
flashcards.back: maxSurge: how many extra Pods above the desired count can exist during rollout. maxUnavailable: how many Pods can be down at once. Both accept absolute numbers or percentages.

flashcards.front: Command to roll back a Deployment to the previous revision?
flashcards.back: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>  (add --to-revision=N to target a specific revision from rollout history).
Liveness: kills and restarts the container if it fails. Readiness: removes the Pod from Service endpoints if it fails (does not restart).

questions.q: Contoso plans to deploy Microsoft Teams. Network engineers must verify that every branch office can reach the required Teams media endpoints with the lowest possible round-trip latency. Which Microsoft-recommended tool runs from each branch and reports network quality against the closest Microsoft network edge?
choices: Microsoft Remote Connectivity Analyzer (testconnectivity.microsoft.com)
Microsoft 365 network connectivity test tool (connectivity.office.com)
Network Planner in the Teams admin center
Call Quality Dashboard (CQD)
questions.explanation: The Microsoft 365 network connectivity test tool at connectivity.office.com is run from a representative client at each office. It identifies the closest Microsoft network edge, measures latency, jitter, packet loss and DNS resolution, and flags whether traffic is being backhauled. Network Planner sizes bandwidth from a profile but does not run live connectivity tests. The Remote Connectivity Analyzer targets Exchange and Teams federation tests rather than per-site media quality. CQD reports historical call telemetry after Teams is in use.

questions.q: You are preparing a hybrid migration from Skype for Business Server on-premises to Microsoft Teams. Existing Skype users must keep their contacts and federation while you progressively move them to TeamsOnly. Which coexistence mode must you assign at the tenant or user level so that users continue to receive chats and calls in Skype until they are migrated?
choices: Islands — both clients run side-by-side for the same user
SfBOnly — Teams collaboration is disabled completely
SfBWithTeamsCollab — Teams is used only for channels
TeamsOnly — Teams becomes the sole client for the user
questions.explanation: SfBWithTeamsCollab keeps chat, calling and meetings in Skype for Business while enabling Microsoft Teams for channel-based collaboration. It is the standard staging mode for a hybrid migration: users keep contacts and federation in Skype while admins onboard them to Teams gradually. Islands lets both clients run for the same user and is appropriate only for greenfield pilots, not hybrid migrations. SfBOnly turns Teams off entirely. TeamsOnly is the post-migration end state, not the staging mode.

questions.q: A compliance officer at Fabrikam must prevent members of the Sales team from sending chat messages to people in the Research team, while still allowing both groups to talk to everyone else in the organization. Which Microsoft Teams feature meets this requirement with the least administrative effort?
choices: Sensitivity labels applied to the underlying Microsoft 365 Groups
Information barriers with two segments and a block policy between them
External access (federation) restrictions in Teams settings
A retention policy that deletes chats between the two groups
questions.explanation: Information barriers (IB) are designed precisely for ethical-wall scenarios. You define two segments based on Microsoft Entra attributes (Sales and Research), then create a block policy between them. Teams enforces IB across one-to-one chats, group chats, calls and team membership. Sensitivity labels protect documents and group settings but do not block chat between people. External access governs federation with other tenants, not internal users. Retention policies retain or delete content; they cannot prevent the communication from occurring.

questions.q: You must allow employees of partnerco.com to chat with your users in Microsoft Teams, but you must block every other domain from federating with your tenant. In the Teams admin center under External access, which configuration enforces this requirement?
choices: Turn external access off, then add partnerco.com to the Blocked domains list
Set Allow all external domains, then add partnerco.com to the Allowed domains list
Set Block all external domains except specific domains, then add partnerco.com to Allowed domains
Enable Guest access and invite each partnerco.com user as a guest in your tenant
questions.explanation: External access (federation) controls chat and calling with other Teams or Skype tenants. To allow exactly one partner domain you switch external access to the Block-all-except mode and add partnerco.com to the Allowed list — every other domain is automatically blocked. The Blocked domains list works the opposite way (allow all except listed). Guest access is a different feature that gives external users an identity inside your tenant so they can join teams; it does not federate native chat between separate tenants and would not be the least-effort option for everyday partner messaging.

nodes.title: Automation and IaC: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) means defining your servers, networks, databases in version-controlled config files instead of clicking around a console. Pipelines automate the apply step. The combination is what makes cloud reproducible.

flashcards.front: What is the value of declarative IaC?
flashcards.back: You describe the desired state ('I want 3 EC2 instances in this VPC'), the tool figures out how to get there. Reruns are idempotent — applying the same code twice doesn't double anything. State drift (someone clicked in the console) is detected on the next plan/diff.

flashcards.front: Terraform vs CloudFormation vs Bicep — what's different?
flashcards.back: Terraform: cloud-agnostic, HCL syntax, plan/apply workflow, huge ecosystem. CloudFormation: AWS-only, YAML/JSON, native rollback. Bicep: Azure-only, cleaner DSL on top of ARM. Pick the cloud-native tool if you're single-cloud; Terraform if multi-cloud or your team prefers HCL.

flashcards.front: What is a CI/CD pipeline for infrastructure?
flashcards.back: Same as for app code: commit → run linter (tflint) → plan / diff → require approval → apply. Production typically has a manual approval gate; lower environments auto-apply. Plan output is reviewed in the PR so a destructive change is caught before merge.

flashcards.front: Why is mutable infrastructure considered an anti-pattern?
flashcards.back: Mutable: SSH in, run apt-get, edit configs, server drifts from its template. Two 'identical' servers slowly diverge → snowflakes → 'works on this instance only' bugs. Immutable: bake a fresh AMI / image, replace the running instance, the old one is destroyed. Painful upfront, trivial to roll back, no drift.

questions.q: Front-line workers at a retail chain need a simplified Teams experience that hides most apps and pins Walkie Talkie, Shifts, Tasks, and Approvals to the navigation bar. Which Teams admin center policy directly controls which apps appear, in what order, on the user's app bar?
choices: App permission policy
App setup policy
Teams policy
Messaging policy
questions.explanation: App setup policies define which apps are pinned to the Teams app bar (rail/navigation), the pinning order, and whether users can pin additional apps. They are the correct tool to standardize the Walkie Talkie / Shifts / Tasks / Approvals layout for front-line workers. App permission policies control whether an app is allowed at all (allow/block lists across Microsoft, third-party and custom apps) but do not pin anything. Teams policies govern discovery and channel settings. Messaging policies govern chat features like edit, delete, giphy, and read receipts.

questions.q: Your organization assigns Microsoft Teams Phone Standard licenses to 200 users in Germany. You need each user to receive an inbound PSTN number from Microsoft that is local to a German city, and Microsoft must provide the upstream PSTN connectivity. Which calling solution should you implement?
choices: Direct Routing with a certified Session Border Controller
Operator Connect with a participating operator
Microsoft Calling Plans with phone numbers from Microsoft
Teams Phone Mobile with a participating mobile operator
questions.explanation: Microsoft Calling Plans give the user a PSTN number provisioned directly by Microsoft, who also acts as the PSTN carrier. Where Calling Plans are available (Germany is in scope) this is the simplest path for tenant-issued numbers with no carrier contract. Direct Routing requires you to bring an SBC and a third-party SIP trunk. Operator Connect uses a third-party operator who supplies the numbers and SIP trunk; Microsoft is not the carrier. Teams Phone Mobile binds the user's mobile SIM to Teams via an operator and is not a tenant-issued number from Microsoft.

questions.q: A meeting organizer reports that anonymous participants from a partner organization are joining her Teams meetings and presenting before she is ready. You must change the default so that everyone who is not signed in to your tenant lands in the lobby for every meeting in the organization, while authenticated colleagues continue to bypass the lobby. Which Teams admin-center setting do you modify?
choices: A meeting policy — Who can bypass the lobby = People in my organization
A messaging policy — Allow anonymous users to start a meeting = Off
Meeting settings (org-wide) — Anonymous users can join a meeting = Off
A live events policy — Who can join scheduled live events = Specific users
questions.explanation: Meeting policies are applied per user or per organizer and include the Who can bypass the lobby setting. Setting it to People in my organization forces every anonymous or external attendee through the lobby while authenticated tenant users continue to join directly. The org-wide Meeting settings toggle for anonymous join blocks anonymous join entirely, which is more restrictive than required. The messaging policy and live events policy do not control lobby behaviour for regular Teams meetings.

questions.q: An admin must give a remote PowerShell script the right to add and remove members from a team called Marketing Campaign. The principle of least privilege applies and the script must continue working even if the admin who creates it later leaves. Which approach should the admin use?
choices: Sign the script with the admin's personal account using Connect-MicrosoftTeams interactively
Add the service account to the team as an Owner and use Connect-MicrosoftTeams with that account
Register an Entra ID application, grant the Microsoft Graph TeamMember.ReadWrite.All application permission with admin consent, and authenticate with a certificate
Use the Teams admin role with a shared mailbox username and password stored in the script
questions.explanation: Unattended Graph automation should run as a registered Entra ID application authenticated with a client certificate (or managed identity). Granting the application the TeamMember.ReadWrite.All application permission, after admin consent, scopes the script narrowly to membership operations and survives any single admin leaving. Personal interactive sign-in is not suitable for unattended automation. Owning a team gives only that team's scope but binds it to a service account whose credentials still need to be protected. Storing username and password in the script violates Microsoft's modern-auth guidance and least privilege.

nodes.title: Troubleshooting methodology: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A structured troubleshooting process beats random guessing every time. The classic flow: identify the problem precisely, form a theory, test it, fix, verify, document. Most exams test that you know the flow AND can spot the layer at which the symptom originates.

flashcards.back: CompTIA's 6-step: (1) Identify the problem (gather symptoms, questions to user, recent changes). (2) Establish a theory of probable cause. (3) Test the theory. (4) Plan and implement the fix. (5) Verify full system functionality, apply preventive measures. (6) Document everything.

flashcards.front: Top-down vs bottom-up troubleshooting on a network problem.
flashcards.back: Top-down: start at the application layer and work down — does the browser work? DNS? TCP? Routing? Bottom-up: start at the physical layer — is the cable plugged in? Link light? IP? When you suspect physical/cable, bottom-up is faster. When the user has 'a website is broken', top-down is faster.

Almost every production incident traces back to a recent change — a deploy, a config push, a vendor patch, a cert rotation. 'It was working yesterday' tells you to check today's change-log before forming an exotic theory. Recent changes are the highest-priors of the bug space.

Bisect the path between symptom and cause. If 10 hops between client and server, test hop 5. Good → problem is past hop 5. Bad → problem is before. Two more bisections narrow it to one hop. Faster than checking every link sequentially when the chain is long.

questions.q: A trainer needs to invite 1,200 external attendees to a one-time keynote. Attendees must register in advance, receive a unique join link, and the producer must be able to manage what the audience sees. The recording must remain available afterward. Which Microsoft Teams meeting type should the trainer schedule?
choices: A standard Teams meeting with Lobby = Everyone bypasses the lobby
A Teams webinar with attendee registration
A Teams live event broadcast
A Teams channel meeting in a public team
questions.explanation: Teams live events are the broadcast format designed for one-to-many, structured productions with a producer/presenter workflow, audience Q&A separate from chat, and a recording produced at the end. They support up to 10,000 attendees and clearly separate the audience from the production team. Webinars cap below this audience size and put attendees in a meeting where they can be promoted; they are best for smaller registration-driven sessions but do not match the requirement for a producer-controlled broadcast at this scale. Standard meetings and channel meetings have neither the scale nor the producer workflow.

questions.q: You publish a custom line-of-business app to the Teams catalog and want it pre-installed for the Helpdesk department only, without users having to discover it in the store. Which combination of policies and settings achieves this?
choices: An app permission policy that blocks the app for everyone except Helpdesk
An app setup policy with the app added to Installed apps, then assign the policy to the Helpdesk group
A messaging policy with the app added as a default message extension
A custom Teams template with the app pinned, then have Helpdesk users create a team from the template
questions.explanation: App setup policies have an Installed apps list as well as a Pinned apps list. Adding the line-of-business app to Installed apps and assigning the policy to the Helpdesk group (via policy assignment or group policy assignment) causes Teams to install the app automatically for those users on next launch — no store discovery required. App permission policies only allow or block apps; they cannot pre-install anything. Messaging policies do not install apps. Teams templates apply when someone creates a team, not when a user signs in to Teams.

questions.q: After enabling Microsoft Teams calling for a pilot, you must investigate a user's repeated complaints about poor audio quality during 1:1 calls over the past two weeks. You need per-call telemetry showing jitter, packet loss, round-trip time and the network path. Which Teams admin tool should you open?
choices: Network Planner
Call Analytics for the specific user
Call Quality Dashboard (CQD)
Real-time analytics (in-meeting)
questions.explanation: Call Analytics is the per-user, per-call diagnostic view in the Teams admin center. For each call you see device, network, jitter, packet loss, round-trip time, and the path from client to media relay — exactly the data needed to root-cause a single user's complaints. CQD aggregates organization-wide trends across many calls and is the right tool for capacity planning or regional issues, not a single user's history. Network Planner sizes bandwidth before deployment. Real-time analytics is limited to a meeting that is currently in progress.

questions.q: Your security team requires that every new Microsoft 365 group created from Microsoft Teams must have its display name prefixed with the department code (for example, FIN- or HR-) so that downstream DLP rules can target groups by department. You also want only members of an Entra ID security group named Team-Creators to be able to create new teams. Which two configurations are required? (Choose two.)
choices: Configure a Microsoft 365 Groups naming policy with a prefix attribute, then restrict group creation to the Team-Creators security group
Configure a Teams messaging policy that blocks team creation for users outside Team-Creators
Apply a sensitivity label that adds a prefix to the team's display name on creation
Configure a Teams policy with the AllowCreateUpdateChannels setting disabled, then restrict creation in the SharePoint admin center
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 Groups naming policy (configured in Entra ID) supports a prefix or suffix sourced from a string or an attribute and is enforced on every group created via Teams, Outlook, Planner, etc. Restricting group creation to a security group is also done in Entra ID (Groups settings — Users can create Microsoft 365 groups in the directory = No, then specify the allowed security group). Together these two settings deliver the naming standard and the creation control. Messaging policies and Teams policies do not gate group creation. Sensitivity labels can enforce privacy and external sharing on groups but do not rename them. Channel creation settings do not affect team creation.
